hello @philb89 - I'm afraid the "save location edits" is broken.  When I edit "Blue-3 EW Attack", it's the formatted HTML that gets stored in the saved message, not the GeoJSON.  

**Update:** No, that's wrong.  Saving an edit works, it's cancelling a location edit that fails.  If I edit EW-Attack, then cancel the location-edit, but still save the updated message, then the plain text gets stored. This is because there is nothing in `pendingLocationData`.  So, the handler for `cancel edit location` should push the original GeoJSON to the save handler.  Experimenting with this.

Note: The existing solution relied on the `pendingLocationData` state object.    In `PlanningMessagesList`, we used to intercept the `saveMessage`, and replace the location (pretty HTML) data with the stored `pendingLocation` data. Somehow we have lost the code that updates `pendingLocationData`.

But, I do think we have  an opportunity for a more robust solution now.  It would work like this:
- location editor component has hidden text component `hiddenStore`.  On load (setValue(), the GeoJSON from `location` gets put into there, before the text area gets written with the human-readable text.  When `Edit` is clicked for the location component, a callback is provided that, when called, updates the contents of `hiddenStore` with the new GeoJSON, and updates the human-readable text.  When `getValue()` is called for location-editor, it returns the GeoJSON from hiddenStore, not the human-readable text.

This avoids the need for `pendingLocationData` in the parent classes.

issues.title: More fixes for LocationEditor
issues.body:
Some steps to complete the location editor are recorded [here](https://twitter.com/RishiSunak/status/1605964002143522816)

Copied below:

Ok, but I _think_ we still need some processing like that.  We need to store the current GeoJSON data in the form (somewhere - maybe in the `location-editor`, or `DOM`), and we need to re-format the GeoJSON in human-readable form. 

We have these requirements. When the form contains a `location-editor`:
1. store the `PlannedActivityGeometry[]` JS array 
2. call a `render` function to convert the array to human readable `<ul>` list, display this as read-only in the `div`
3. provide an `Edit` button, when the form is editable
4. when the `Edit` button is clicked, provide the raw `PlannedActivityGeometry[]` array to the callback
5. when `Save` is clicked during location edit, store the new `PlannedActivityGeometry[]`, and re-do the `Render` function
6. when `Save` is clicked for the JSON-Editor, push the `current` value of of `PlannedActivityGeometry` back into the location field of the results object.
